aboutParagraph: A glossary of Minecraft speedrunning terms, strategies, tools, and community language.

terms.name: Any%
terms.definition: Any% is a speedrun category with no required completion percentage; the runner reaches the endpoint defined by that board's rules as quickly as possible. In Minecraft: Java Edition Any% Glitchless, timing ends when the credits begin after the runner enters the exit End portal—not when the Ender Dragon merely dies. `Any%` alone does not specify Random Seed, Set Seed, version group, or glitch rules.

terms.name: Atum
terms.definition: Atum is a Minecraft: Java Edition speedrunning utility mod that streamlines the repeated world-creation and reset flow used for RSG attempts. Its shortcuts reduce menu work between seeds, letting runners spend more time evaluating and playing worlds. Supported versions and leaderboard legality depend on the current rules and approved-mod list.

terms.name: Bastion
terms.definition: Bastion is the common MCSR name for a Bastion Remnant, a Nether structure added in Minecraft 1.16. In Java 1.16.1 RSG and Ranked, a bastion concentrates gold blocks, piglins, and chests so one practiced route can produce pearls, obsidian, string, and Fire Resistance. Bridge, Housing, Stables, and Treasure have different geometry, hazards, and resource routes.

terms.name: Bastion Route
terms.definition: A Bastion Route is a practiced path through one of the four Bastion Remnant layouts. A route coordinates gold collection, chest looting, piglin positioning, and bartering so the runner can obtain needed resources quickly and safely. Bridge, Housing, Stables, and Treasure bastions require different routes, especially in Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG and Ranked runs.

terms.name: Blaze
terms.definition: A Blaze is a hostile Nether mob and the source of Blaze Rods. In MCSR, runners usually fight Blazes at a Nether Fortress spawner because the rods are required to craft Eyes of Ender. MCSR Ranked standardizes Blaze Rod drops and spawner timing so both racers receive comparable RNG.

terms.name: Blaze Bed

media.title: Blaze bedding tutorial
media.caption: Open and enclosed Blaze Bed setups

terms.name: Blaze Rods
terms.definition: Blaze Rods are items dropped by Blazes. Each rod crafts into two Blaze Powder, and one powder combines with one Ender Pearl to make an Eye of Ender. Speedrunners obtain rods in Nether Fortresses; piglins do not barter Blaze Rods.

terms.name: Blind
Bridge Bastion
Bucket Portal
Buried Treasure
terms.definition: Buried Treasure is a single hidden chest generated beneath beach or ocean terrain. In Java 1.16 RSG, its food, iron, gold, and occasional diamonds can provide a compact early-game resource route. Runners may follow a shipwreck map or use the version-specific Mapless technique to identify the correct treasure chunk.

terms.name: Calculated Travel
Classic
terms.definition: In MCSR Ranked, Classic refers to completing a winning route without entering a Bastion. Outside Ranked, runners may use the word more loosely for older or no-bastion Java 1.16 routes, which can barter with ordinary piglins for pearls but still obtain Blaze Rods from Blazes. Because the informal meaning varies, a definition or run commentary should state the intended context.

terms.name: Desert Temple
terms.definition: A Desert Temple is an Overworld structure with four loot chests above a concealed TNT trap. A runner can drop safely into the chamber, break the pressure plate, and take materials such as iron, gold, obsidian, string, or food when the seed makes the detour worthwhile. The TNT itself can also support specialized portal or routing strategies.

terms.name: Divine Travel
Educated Travel
Elo
terms.definition: Elo is the rating used by MCSR Ranked to match players of similar skill and order its competitive ladder. Winning normally raises a player's Elo and losing lowers it, with the change influenced by the opponent's rating. The official styling is `Elo`, not the acronym `ELO`.

terms.name: End Entry
terms.definition: End Entry is the moment a runner enters an activated End portal and loads the End dimension. It is a common split and run-evaluation milestone because the remaining time is dominated by island access, dragon behavior, and the chosen fight strategy. End Entry is not the Any% finish; the run ends only after the required exit-portal transition begins the credits.

terms.name: Ender Pearl
terms.definition: An Ender Pearl is a throwable item that teleports the player to where it lands and is also an ingredient in an Eye of Ender. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, runners commonly obtain pearls by bartering with piglins, usually at a bastion. Extra pearls can also save travel time or enable safer movement.

terms.name: Eye of Ender
terms.definition: An Eye of Ender is crafted from one Ender Pearl and one Blaze Powder. Thrown eyes travel toward the nearest Stronghold and may drop or break; runners measure their direction to navigate or triangulate. Eyes also fill the twelve End portal frames, although some frames can generate already filled.

terms.name: F3
terms.definition: F3 usually means Minecraft: Java Edition's debug screen and related key combinations. Coordinates, facing, chunk position, entity counts, and profiler views support techniques such as stronghold measurement, Mapless, Pie Chart routing, and Microlensing. The fields and shortcuts vary by game version, and a leaderboard can restrict particular debug uses, so the run's rules remain authoritative.

terms.name: Filtered Seed
terms.definition: A Filtered Seed is randomly generated and accepted only when it satisfies declared conditions. Filtering can reduce uncompetitive starts without revealing a memorized Set Seed route: FSG generators apply category-specific filters, while MCSR Ranked constructs matches from separately filtered Overworld and Nether seeds. The exact guarantees come from the format's current filter, not from the phrase `filtered seed` by itself.

terms.name: Flintless Portal
terms.definition: A Flintless Portal is a Nether portal ignited without flint and steel. The usual setup places a flammable block beside the portal opening and uses nearby lava to create or spread fire into the frame. It preserves iron or rescues a route with no flint, but its ignition timing is less direct than using flint and steel.

terms.name: Forced Perch
terms.definition: Forced Perch describes MCSR Ranked's extra limit on extreme Ender Dragon perch waits. Alongside standardized perch rolls, Ranked makes the dragon perch when the probability of having avoided every perch falls below its documented threshold. It reduces very long waits, but player position and actions can still change dragon phases, so opponents are not guaranteed identical perch times.

terms.name: Fortress Navigation
FSG
terms.definition: FSG means Filtered Seed Glitchless, a format where an approved generator searches for random seeds that satisfy declared conditions before the runner receives one. The filter reduces selected early-game variance without revealing the full route, so FSG is different from both unrestricted RSG and practicing a known Set Seed. Exact filters and verification requirements belong to the category's rules.

terms.name: Glitchless
terms.definition: Glitchless is a rules classification that excludes a category's prohibited glitches while allowing ordinary game mechanics and explicitly permitted techniques. It does not mean the run avoids every bug-like behavior, and different games or Minecraft boards may draw the boundary differently. For Minecraft Java Any%, the current leaderboard rules—not the label alone—define what is legal.

terms.name: Half Bow
terms.definition: Half Bow is an End-fight strategy that destroys some—but not all—End crystals with a bow before waiting for the dragon to perch. Reducing the number of live crystals can improve the dragon's chance to choose a perch approach, while leaving others saves shooting time. The tradeoff is that breaking a crystal can send the dragon into a strafe, so timing and the chosen towers matter.

terms.name: Housing Bastion
Hypermodern
terms.definition: Hypermodern is a selective, reset-heavy route family for Java 1.16.1 RSG. It prioritizes strong coastal or Mapless starts, rapid Nether Entry, efficient Bastion and fortress play, Nether Travel, and a highly optimized End fight instead of completing every merely playable seed. The term describes that RSG approach; it is not a universal label for newer Minecraft versions or Ranked's filtered-seed format.

terms.name: IGT
terms.definition: IGT means In-Game Time, a timing method that counts the game's active run state rather than every second of wall-clock time. Minecraft Java Edition rules define which loading, pausing, and frozen periods are excluded, and approved tools such as SpeedRunIGT can record the relevant timer and events for verification. The exact start, finish, and exclusions are category rules—not a universal property of the on-screen timer.

terms.name: Lava Pool
terms.definition: A Lava Pool is a group of exposed lava source blocks that can supply a quickly cast Nether portal. In RSG, runners evaluate whether the pool has enough accessible sources, nearby water, and safe terrain for a Bucket Portal. A convenient pool can produce a very fast Nether Entry, while an awkward or incomplete one may cost more time than another route.

terms.name: Leaderboard
terms.definition: A Leaderboard lists accepted run times for one category and its variables. Minecraft Java Edition runners submit video and required files for moderator review; accepted placements are comparable only within the same rules, version, difficulty, seed type, and timing method. Because rulings and records change, the live board is the source of truth rather than a hard-coded time or holder.

terms.name: LiveSplit
terms.definition: LiveSplit is an open-source speedrun timer that records segment splits and compares attempts with saved runs. Minecraft runners can use it to display pace and personal-best comparisons, but the visible timer is not automatically the official leaderboard time; the category's timing rules still control.

terms.name: Magma Ravine
terms.definition: A Magma Ravine is an underwater ravine whose magma blocks and exposed deep lava make an ocean Nether-entry route possible. Runners use the bubbles for air, collect iron or doors as needed, and cast a portal from the submerged lava. It is especially valuable on ocean spawns where surface lava is scarce and a nearby shipwreck can supply resources.

terms.name: Mapless
Matchmaking
terms.definition: Matchmaking is the MCSR Ranked system that pairs queued players for a head-to-head race. It searches around a player's current rating and can broaden the acceptable range while the queue continues, balancing similarly rated opponents against wait time. Matchmaking creates the opponent pairing; the match itself still uses Ranked's seed and RNG rules.

terms.name: MCSR Ranked
terms.definition: MCSR Ranked is a Minecraft: Java Edition 1.16.1 Fabric mod and competitive format for live head-to-head speedrun races. Standard matches give both players equivalent filtered dimension seeds and standardized sequences for selected RNG, while each runner still makes and executes an independent route. Matchmaking, placement games, and Elo organize ranked play; Casual, Private Rooms, and Weekly Race provide other ways to use the format.

terms.name: Microlensing

media.caption: Bastion microlensing with F3 entity counts

terms.name: Minecraft Speedrunning
terms.definition: Minecraft speedrunning is completing a defined Minecraft objective under a category's rules as quickly as possible. A prominent example is Java Edition Any% Glitchless Random Seed, where the runner begins an unknown world, reaches the End, defeats the dragon, and enters the exit portal. Bedrock Edition, Set Seed, older versions, extensions, and competitive formats can use different endpoints and allowed techniques.

terms.name: Multi-Instance
terms.definition: Multi-Instance is an RSG setup that runs several separate Minecraft clients so worlds can generate in parallel and the runner can evaluate more starts. Tools such as WorldPreview help present those worlds, while Atum or reset controls streamline the transition between attempts. Official rules impose installation, recording, resource, and configuration requirements; SeedQueue is a distinct one-instance approach.

terms.name: Nether Entry
terms.definition: Nether Entry is the moment a runner completes the portal transition and loads the Nether. It is one of the most useful early split points because it summarizes the spawn evaluation, resource collection, and portal construction that came before it. The entry's coordinates and nearby terrain also determine the first Nether routing decision.

terms.name: Ninjabrain Bot
terms.definition: Ninjabrain Bot is an external stronghold calculator for Minecraft: Java Edition speedrunning. The runner supplies precise Eye of Ender measurements and uncertainty information; the tool combines them with stronghold-generation probabilities to estimate target coordinates and confidence. It supports Triangulation and Calculated Travel but does not replace accurate inputs, and its permitted version and settings must match current category rules.

terms.name: Obsidian
terms.definition: Obsidian is the block used to build Nether portal frames. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, runners commonly obtain it from bastion chests and piglin bartering rather than mining it. Extra obsidian enables a second portal for Nether Travel and can also be useful during the End fight.

terms.name: One Cycle

media.title: One-cycle Ender Dragon tutorial
media.caption: Bed timing for a one-cycle finish

terms.name: Pace
terms.definition: Pace describes how an attempt is progressing toward a time goal such as a personal best or world record. Runners infer pace from the current time, route state, resources, and splits. Being on a particular pace is a projection, not a guarantee of the final time.

terms.name: PB
terms.definition: PB means personal best: a runner's fastest valid completion in a particular category, ruleset, and timing method. A runner can therefore have separate PBs for RSG, Set Seed, different version groups, or different timing methods.

terms.name: Perch

media.title: How the Ender Dragon perches
media.caption: Dragon perch cues and bed setup

terms.name: Pie Chart
terms.definition: The Pie Chart is Minecraft: Java Edition's debug profiler graph, opened with `F3+1` in current versions and historically with `Shift+F3`. Runners navigate profiler sections and compare readings across render distances or chunk boundaries to infer structures, including the treasure-chunk step of Mapless. This family of uses is often called pie-ray or piedar; menu paths and valid procedures are version- and category-specific.

terms.name: Piglin Bartering
terms.definition: Piglin Bartering is giving gold ingots to adult piglins in exchange for randomized items. In Java Edition 1.16.1 RSG, barters can provide Ender Pearls, obsidian, string, and fire resistance, making bastion routing central to many runs. Later 1.16 versions use a different barter table, and Blaze Rods never come from bartering.

terms.name: Placement Match
terms.definition: A Placement Match is one of the initial MCSR Ranked games used to establish a player's starting competitive rating for a season. Its result contributes to the system's estimate before a normal visible rank is settled. The number and rating effect of placements can change between seasons, so the current Ranked documentation is authoritative.

terms.name: Portal Room
terms.definition: The Portal Room is the Stronghold room containing the twelve-frame End portal and a silverfish spawner. Runners reach it through stronghold navigation, remove or avoid the spawner, fill every empty frame with an Eye of Ender, and enter the activated portal. Existing filled frames reduce how many eyes the run must craft and preserve more pearls for movement or the End fight.

terms.name: Random Seed
terms.definition: Random Seed is a speedrun seed type in which the seed input is left blank and the runner does not choose the world in advance. The official Java rules require a blank seed field. Random Seed describes seed knowledge; RSG additionally specifies a glitchless ruleset.

terms.name: Reset
terms.definition: A Reset abandons the current attempt and starts another world. RSG runners compare the seed's spawn, resources, structures, execution, and current pace with the threshold for their route; resetting early trades a weak attempt for another chance at a stronger seed. Approved tools can shorten world creation, but current Java rules still control automation, recording, and when a reset action may be triggered.

terms.name: RNG
terms.definition: RNG means Random Number Generation: the systems that choose uncertain outcomes such as world features, loot, barters, drops, spawns, and dragon behavior. Runners cannot control every roll, but they can route around risk, keep backups, and judge when a seed is worth continuing. MCSR Ranked standardizes selected RNG events; normal RSG does not remove their variance.

terms.name: RNG Standardization
terms.definition: RNG Standardization is MCSR Ranked's system for giving both players matched sequences for selected random events. Documented examples include piglin barters, entity and block drops, Eye of Ender breaks, spawner attempts, and parts of Ender Dragon behavior. It reduces unequal extreme rolls, but it does not make player actions identical, eliminate every random event, or guarantee the same route outcome.

terms.name: RSG
terms.definition: RSG means Random Seed Glitchless. The runner leaves the seed field blank, starts an unknown world, and completes the objective without techniques prohibited by that board's glitchless rules. The abbreviation combines seed knowledge with a rule classification; edition, category, difficulty, and version still matter, so `Java 1.16.1 Any% RSG` is more precise than `RSG` alone.

terms.name: RTA
terms.definition: RTA means Real-Time Attack and measures elapsed real time from start to finish, normally including loads and pauses unless a category says otherwise. It contrasts with In-Game Time. Minecraft Java Edition leaderboard categories commonly use IGT, so runners should not assume an RTA display is the submitted time.

terms.name: Ruined Portal
terms.definition: A Ruined Portal is an incomplete Nether portal structure with obsidian, crying obsidian, gold blocks, and a nearby loot chest. When enough usable frame blocks and replacement obsidian are available, a runner can repair it for a fast Nether Entry instead of casting a full portal. Crying obsidian cannot fill a normal portal frame, so the exact layout and chest contents determine its value.

terms.name: Seed
terms.definition: A seed is the value Minecraft uses as an input when generating a world. Reusing a seed with the same relevant game version and settings can reproduce major terrain and structures, which makes chosen seeds suitable for Set Seed competition. Random Seed runs leave the seed field blank instead.

terms.name: SeedQueue
terms.definition: SeedQueue is a reset-management mod that prepares multiple random worlds in the background and presents them through one Minecraft instance. It reduces generation downtime without running several playable clients at once, making it an alternative to traditional Multi-Instance setups. Legal runs must use the approved version and follow current rules for configuration, resource limits, world selection, and recording.

terms.name: Set Seed
terms.definition: Set Seed is a speedrun seed type in which the runner deliberately enters and knows the world seed before the attempt. Repetition makes exact movement, crafting, structure routes, and backups highly optimizable. `SSG` commonly expands to Set Seed Glitchless on Minecraft Any% boards, but `Set Seed` by itself describes seed selection and does not automatically specify glitch rules, version, or endpoint.

terms.name: Shipwreck
terms.definition: A Shipwreck is an ocean or beach structure with up to three chest types containing supplies, valuables, and sometimes a Buried Treasure map. In Java 1.16 RSG, a strong wreck can provide food, iron, wood, and a route to treasure from one compact stop. Its orientation and missing sections determine which chests actually generated, so runners identify the layout before committing time.

terms.name: Spawn
terms.definition: Spawn is the location where the player first enters a new world. In RSG, runners quickly evaluate nearby terrain, structures, food, iron, and Nether-entry options before deciding whether to continue or reset. Ranked starts are generated under its own filtering and standardization rules.

terms.name: Speedrun.com
terms.definition: Speedrun.com is the platform hosting the main community-run Minecraft: Java Edition leaderboards. The game pages publish categories, variables, rules, resources, and accepted results; volunteer moderators review submitted evidence and required files. It is not operated by Mojang, and a runner should read the current category rules before recording because verification requirements can change.

terms.name: SpeedRunIGT
terms.definition: SpeedRunIGT is an open-source Minecraft: Java Edition timing mod that records in-game time and speedrun events inside the client. It can automate category timing, splits, and run metadata while excluding periods that current rules do not count. Because accepted versions and settings can change, runners should match the mod and configuration required by the leaderboard they submit to.

terms.name: Split
terms.definition: A split is the cumulative time recorded when a runner reaches a chosen checkpoint; a segment is the time between two splits. MCSR runners might split on Nether entry, Nether exit, End entry, and the final exit-portal transition, but layouts are personal rather than an official fixed list. Timer tools compare current splits against a PB or another target.

terms.name: Stables Bastion
StandardSettings
terms.definition: StandardSettings is an open-source Minecraft speedrunning mod that applies a known set of category-appropriate game options when creating worlds. Consistent difficulty, commands, and related settings reduce accidental invalid runs and make repeated attempts easier to audit. Runners still need the version and configuration required by the current rules; installing the mod alone does not establish legality.

terms.name: Starter Staircase
terms.definition: The Starter Staircase is the spiral-stair room from which a Java Stronghold's generation begins. Eyes of Ender lead toward this starting area rather than directly to the Portal Room, so runners use its position and facing as the reference point for structure navigation. Recognizing it helps separate intentional navigation from searching every corridor at random.

terms.name: Stronghold

media.title: Stronghold navigation tutorial
media.caption: Stronghold navigation from the Starter Staircase

terms.name: Stronghold Navigation
terms.definition: Stronghold Navigation is the technique of using Java Stronghold generation rules to reach the Portal Room efficiently. Starting from the Starter Staircase, runners track room orientation, doorways, dead ends, and generation branches instead of exploring every path equally. The skill matters because a close stronghold exit can still lose substantial time if the interior is searched without a plan.

Triangulation

terms.name: Village
terms.definition: A Village is an Overworld structure that can combine several early speedrun resources: beds, food or hay bales, wood, crafting blocks, and an Iron Golem. Java 1.16 RSG runners often kill the golem for bucket-and-flint-and-steel iron, collect beds for the dragon fight, and leave quickly for a portal. The biome, house layout, and nearby lava determine whether the route is efficient.

terms.name: WorldPreview
terms.definition: WorldPreview is an open-source Minecraft: Java Edition mod that displays a generated world's initial view before the player commits to loading it normally. In approved multi-reset workflows, the preview helps runners evaluate seeds while other worlds generate. Its legal use, visible information, and compatible versions are defined by the current category rules and approved-mod list.

terms.name: WR
terms.definition: WR means world record: the fastest accepted valid time on a specified category and variables leaderboard at a given point in time. For Minecraft, edition, seed type, glitch rules, version group, and timing method can all distinguish records, so the live leaderboard is more reliable than a hard-coded holder or time.

terms.name: Zero Cycle
